text:
ophelia-infra: Heads up — seeing a burst of GPU nodes stuck in Provisioning in ap-south after the prod firewall tighten landed. Boot logs show KMS Decrypt failures. Suspect egress blocked to keystore privnet endpoint.
ophelia-infra: Snippet from one node:
```
2026-03-21T10:04:12Z ERROR keystore.Decrypt AccessDeniedException: arn:aws:sts::123456:assumed-role/node-join-role not authorized to perform kms:Decrypt on arn:aws:kms:ap-south-1:123456:key/0a1b2c
failed to fetch ephemeral key, retrying...
```
lucy-ops: Confirmed. k8s shows many join attempts 10:03-10:06 stuck. NAT flow logs show outbound SYNs to privnet-host:443 getting RST from SG level. Not a NAT capacity issue.
michael-sre: We should avoid global rollback. Plan: open temporary SG egress rule allowing worker-subnet CIDRs -> keystore privnet-host:443, tag for audit, TTL 30m. Who can approve?
kai-security: That FW change intentionally tightened host CIDR ranges. Exceptions allowed only with audit ticket and explicit TTL <=1h. Provide subnets and justification. Also capture keystore access logs during exception window.
anya-platform: If nodes can't join we'll start launching on-demand in other regions to keep SLAs — this will trigger extra spend and add cross-region latency for customers. Estimate +$1.2k/day if prolonged.
jane-cost: (not in thread) — tagging for cost, but I see jorge-cost in the channel.
jorge-cost: Noted. If we exceed baseline on-demand GPU by 10% I'll auto-open a cost alert. Temporary SG exception is cheaper than cross-region fallbacks; keep it short.
ophelia-infra: Subnets impacted: subnet-0f1e2d3c, subnet-0c3d2e1f. Opening ticket INFRA-9512.
michael-sre: Ran command: ```aws ec2 authorize-security-group-egress --group-id sg-worker-egress --protocol tcp --port 443 --cidr 10.0.0.0/16 --description "keystore-temp-exception INFRA-9512 TTL=30m"```
devon-bot: deploybot: SG rule sg-r-99aa created, annotation TTL=30m, linked INFRA-9512.
lucy-ops: Nodes started registering at 10:09; cluster capacity recovering. Warmpool refill kicked at 10:12.
kai-security: After immediate recovery, we need to avoid repeating this. Proposal: update KMS key policy to explicitly allow kms:Decrypt for the node-join-role with a SourceVPC or SourceIP condition or require sigv4 from privnet endpoint. Also evaluate moving keystore behind Privatelink to simplify SG rules.
michael-sre: We can prototype Privatelink in staging but long lead. Short-term I'd prefer key policy tweak scoped to role + MFA? But KMS doesn't do MFA; we can scope by condition aws:SourceVpce or aws:SourceIp.
anya-platform: Note for runbook: add step that FW rollouts validate keystore egress by running bootstrap smoke on warm-pool nodes before merge. Prevents blast radius.
jorge-cost: Also add in cost matrix: warm-pool buffer sizing vs fallback on-demand cost. Current buffer prevented full outage; but we still lost ~15 minutes capacity — model shows ~6% reduction in throughput.
ophelia-infra: Follow-ups: 1) kai to draft KMS policy change (INFRA-9512-1), 2) platform to add keystore check to pre-roll checklist, 3) ops to record exact timestamps and snapshot keystore audit logs, 4) finance to monitor on-demand spend for 24h.
kai-security: I'll start a PR for key policy conditions and tag for review. Will not remove temporary SG until keypolicy or privatelink is in place.
ophelia-infra: Thanks — closing for now. If it reappears ping me directly. :thumbsup:
